text:
sara: heads up — noticed a p95/p99 tail spike after we pushed runtime v3.14 to canary (5% traffic) ~10m ago. small-seq traffic looks worst.

deploy-bot: deployment completed: runtime-service v3.14 -> canary (5%) at 2026-03-17T12:00:20Z :rocket:

metrics.bot: quick snapshot: p95 went from 120ms -> 420ms, p99 210ms -> 1.2s for seq_len <= 16 paths. Affected region: us-west-2.

kevin: ack. I'm watching graphs. Can you paste a trace id or example request?

sara: sample trace id: trace-0a1b2c (attached flame snippet). Repro steps below.

sara: repro (quick):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood-inference/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-bert-small","input":"short prompt","max_tokens":8}'
```

sara: running that 100qps from a canary agent shows tail latency tailing into >1s occasionally. Longer sequences (>=128) unaffected.

max: interesting — that points at small-batch path. v3.14 included the new scheduler patch (switch to scheduling-v2) and default batching threshold lowered to 1 for micro-batching perf.

elena: @max can you confirm which flag exactly changed? I remember a perf tweak landed that changed aggregator timeout from 2ms -> 10ms?

max: yes — two things in v3.14: scheduler=v2 enabled by default, and BATCH_MIN_TOKENS was changed from 8 -> 1 to favor micro-batching. Also added kernel selection heuristic tweak for short seqs.

oncall-ryan: can we replicate on a canary instance? I can spin up a debug canary with v3.13 vs v3.14 side-by-side and run a load job.

kevin: run this quick k6 job against both variants:
```
k6 run --vus 50 --duration 1m small_seq_test.js --env ENDPOINT=https://<canary-ip>
```
where small_seq_test.js issues 50rps of seq_len 8 requests.

elena: logs from canary instance (snippet):
```
[2026-03-17T12:02:10Z] warn: batch_timer fired after 9ms, batch_size=1, exec_path=short_seq_kernel
[2026-03-17T12:02:11Z] info: kernel_select: short_seq_kernel -> quantized_path
[2026-03-17T12:02:11Z] error: kv-cache lookup miss, cold fill latency=230ms
```

beth: customers pinging support about slow responses for quick lookups — we should prioritize mitigation.

sara: preliminary hypothesis: micro-batch threshold + increased batch timer is increasing serialization overhead for tiny requests, and the kernel heuristic is choosing a slower quantized path for short sequences. explains why long seq unaffected.

max: agreed. Quick mitigation options: 1) rollback scheduling-v2 and flag changes in canary; 2) bump BATCH_MIN_TOKENS back to 8; 3) force short-seq kernel selection to fast path. Which do we want as hotfix?

kevin: safest fast fix: revert BATCH_MIN_TOKENS change at runtime config for canary traffic -> should reduce single-request timer firing. Rollback scheduler might be bigger.

oncall-ryan: I can push a config override to canary pool: set env BATCH_MIN_TOKENS=8 for runtime-service-canary. Doing it now and will monitor.

metrics.bot: config change observed at 12:10:40Z. New canary pool env: BATCH_MIN_TOKENS=8.

metrics.bot: 2m after change: p95 dropped from 420ms -> 160ms, p99 from 1.2s -> 260ms for small-seq traffic. Improvement visible. :thumbsup:

beth: good. Communicate to support we applied a mitigation and we're continuing an investigation, ETA for full fix?

max: next steps: bisect the scheduler change vs kernel heuristic vs batch timer change. I'll create a matrix of variants: (v3.13, v3.14 with scheduler-v1, v3.14 with scheduler-v2 but BATCH_MIN_TOKENS=8, v3.14 kernel-heuristic-rollback). We can run the k6 suite across each.

elena: please also capture pprof CPU hotspots and eBPF traces for the tail events — that will tell whether overhead is in queuing, context switches, or the kernel path.

kevin: logging todo: add short-seq sampling tag so we can track per-request kernel selection decision in traces.

sara: I'll file an internal incident and link this thread. Support message drafted: "We've applied a mitigation to canary to address tail latency for short requests; engineering is bisecting the runtime change. We'll update by EOD."

beth: ping customers impacted list for follow-up. Thanks all.

max: assigning myself to the bisect. Will update with a run matrix and results in this thread.

sara: excellent — marking as monitored.

metrics.bot: final note (12:24:00Z): traffic split remained at 5% canary, but effective latency no longer elevated. continuing to collect data for 2h window.

kevin: follow-up: add a unit/regression test to the runtime CI to simulate high qps short-seq non-batching to avoid regressions.

elena: created issue infra#4521 for the regression test + kernel heuristic review.

max: update: bisect run scheduled in 30m. will report back with diff and candidate PR to revert or patch.

sara: thanks everyone. closing the immediate escalation after mitigation; keep thread open for bisect updates. :white_check_mark:
